requirements.title: Processors have at least one companion processor
requirements.definition: A Fortran processor has one or more companion processors. The companion set can include the Fortran processor itself, so this concept does not by itself require a distinct C compiler, a linker convention, a storage layout or a named external tool.

pending.companion-processor-existence: PENDING no portable Fortran-only introspection reveals the companion set. Future mixed-language fixtures may use companion-specific rules only under Clause 15 or 18 catalogues and must not infer a count from successful Fortran execution.

requirements.oracle: No direct execution oracle is assigned here. Future fixtures observe only the concrete interoperable relation required by their owning Clause 15 or 18 rule.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A pure Fortran program cannot portably distinguish a self companion from a separate processor or enumerate the companion set. Linker names, object formats and toolchain banners are processor dependent.
requirements.dependencies: 15.6.3 covers procedures defined by means other than Fortran; Clause 18 covers C interoperability and C descriptors; 4.2 processor conformance governs the processor concept.

requirements.title: Processors may select among multiple companion processors by processor-dependent means
requirements.definition: If a processor has more than one companion processor, the standard grants processor latitude for the means by which the Fortran processor selects among them. It fixes no portable selector name, priority order, ABI choice, command-line option or header path in this overview.

pending.multiple-companion-selection-permission: PENDING permission record only: no portable oracle requires a particular companion selection among several. Future BIND(C) or CFI tests record the selected toolchain/header profile and assert only relations fixed by Clause 18.

requirements.oracle: This is processor permission, not a required observable behavior. Future valid programs and oracles must be invariant across any companion-selection means the processor provides.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No Fortran-only program can portably require, enumerate or compare a particular selection mechanism among multiple companion processors. Companion choice, ABI naming, object formats, headers, library search order and command-line switches are processor dependent.
requirements.dependencies: 18.3, 18.5 and 18.9 specify concrete C interoperability requirements; 15.6.3 defines non-Fortran procedure definitions; processor dependency terminology is governed by Clause 4.

accounting.rationale: PDF66 defines required companion-processor existence, possible forms and processor-dependent selection among multiple companions; fine units split the obligation and latitude.

A companion processor can be a non-Fortran mechanism, the Fortran processor itself or another Fortran processor. Procedure definition by other means is owned by 15.6.3 and C interoperability by Clause 18.
Processor-dependent selection among multiple companion processors is latitude. This permission record carries no portable selection oracle; concrete interoperation remains with Clause 18.

Defines the document terminology C function for procedures supplied by a non-Fortran companion, without requiring the companion language to be C. Clause 15 and 18 own interoperable procedure requirements.
The note discusses possible ISO C conformance, termination and non-C mechanisms; notes are not normative requirements.

review_rationale: Source registration for 5.4.7-5.4.11 and 5.5-5.5.7 of the Clause 5 overview (batch250). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; restated rules are cross-referenced to their owning catalogues, R516 had no existing tests, and processor-dependent text is latitude. Source accounting only.
